$comment: Per-role model ladder and effort level. ADR-0018 (ladder), ADR-0021 (effort).
One object per role so the two never drift apart: two maps keyed by role
would be a synchronization debt, and this file exists to be a single source.
ladder: ordered by preference. The guard runs the first rung that is not
rate-limited, per the ledger issue labeled model-limits. The LAST rung is
the floor: nothing below it is reachable, so an exhausted ladder means the
agent skips this cycle rather than silently dropping to a weaker model.
An empty ladder means no --model flag: action default, never falls back,
never skipped for model reasons.
The BDFL's rung is a budget decision, not a permission one. ADR-0031
gives the BDFL every role's model and effort choice under the standard
most capable this project can afford. Current choices are the data below;
the allowance incident that established the rule lives in issue #197.
effort: one of low, medium, high, xhigh, max, or empty for the
session default. Available levels depend on the model, which this file
cannot check; an unrecognized value is ignored with a log line rather than
failing the run.
thrift (issue #202): optional per-role ladder/effort override. Absent
means unchanged. agent-guard reads the allowance-state ledger issue
(written by agent-audit) and projects its week-average burn rate against
the next seven-day reset; when the projection misses the reset, it runs
this role at 'thrift' instead of its normal ladder/effort for that one
cycle. No file edit needed either direction: the guard re-projects on
every wake, so restoring the normal tier costs nothing once the
allowance shows slack again. Only roles worth thinning need an entry;
a role already on its floor model has nothing cheaper to fall back to.
The BDFL owns this file (ADR-0031). It lives outside .github/ so changing
it is an ordinary app-token commit, not an admin-PAT workflow push.

bdfl.$comment: Thrift drops the model and keeps the thinking: this seat is 47.3% of the fleet's seven-day projected cost, the largest of any seat. Retries the cheaper model at the normal rung's own effort after #362 moved model and effort together and credited the model. A bet with a written falsification, both tells and the full reasoning in SOURCES.md, 2026-09-19.

curator.$comment: Opus first, sonnet floor: adversarial critique is this seat's entire output, and weak sparring is noise that trains authors to ignore it (ADR-0044). One daily wake, so the raise costs one sonnet-to-opus delta a day; thrift sheds it first.

herald.$comment: Opus floor, no sonnet rung: writing quality for humans is this seat's entire output, and a weaker writer defeats the seat (ADR-0040). Thrift trades that deliberately when the alternative is a dead factory.

researcher.$comment: Opus first: the weekly Saturday wake is the fleet's judgment-densest single session, so the raise costs one sonnet-to-opus delta a week (operator directive, Telegram, 2026-09-01).
